subject: Close timeline failure-mode analysis and contingency actions
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Megan Torres <megan@borealis.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Close timeline failure-mode analysis and contingency actions

Megan — quick note following the technical sync this morning. We ran the timeline against the existing MAP and there are three blockers that, unless mitigated, will push the close beyond your target of 2028-07-05:

1) Evaluation infra availability — your security team is requesting a private VPC for the sandbox and the cloud onboarding ticket is in pending procurement approval (Adam is the approver).
2) Data ingest timing — the sample dataset for the eval is larger than expected; our initial throughput numbers need another 48–72 hours of probing on the private environment.
3) Contract redlines — procurement wants a shorter retention clause and SOC2 evidence before the PO can be cut.

I attached an updated MAP (Borealis_MAP_v3.xlsx) and the risk log (redwood-risk-log-20280621.csv) with the items above logged as high-impact. Proposed mitigations inside: parallelize a reduced-scope eval (3 day smoke) + canary SLA to prove performance, and a temporary data-handling addendum to bridge procurement while SOC2 docs are assembled.

Ask: can your procurement agree to a PO-pre-commit (signature conditional on SOC2 delivery within 15 days) or do we need an executive procurement exception? If neither is possible, we should rebaseline the MAP today and lock the new target with owners.

Thanks — I want to avoid last-minute surprises for our joint exec review next week.

—Markus
Markus Klein | Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
attachments: Borealis_MAP_v3.xlsx, redwood-risk-log-20280621.csv
From: Megan Torres <megan@borealis.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Adam Li <adam.li@borealis.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T11:01:00Z
Subject: Re: Close timeline failure-mode analysis and contingency actions

Markus — thanks for the clear summary and for flagging this early. Short answers up front: procurement will not cut a PO without SOC2 evidence in our file; Adam is out of office until Friday and needs to review the retention language; security wants the private VPC for any dataset > PII-scrubbed samples.

That said, we are willing to consider a phased acceptance approach:
- Phase 1 (acceptance): limited-functionality smoke test on a scrubbed subset (3 business days) inside a secured shared sandbox you provide.
- Phase 2 (full eval): private VPC and end-to-end validation on full sample (5 business days) once procurement and SOC2 are confirmed.

If Redwood can commit to hosting the Phase 1 sandbox (no customer data, only synthetic/scrubbed), I can push Adam for a PO-conditional approval to cover the Phase 1 run. We would still need SOC2 artifacts before moving to Phase 2.

I'll coordinate with Adam but please circulate a one-page MAP delta that calls out Phase 1 deliverables and acceptance criteria so procurement has something concrete.

—Megan
Megan Torres | Head of Data Platforms | Borealis Analytics
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Megan Torres <megan@borealis.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-22T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Close timeline failure-mode analysis and contingency actions

Megan/Markus — technical follow-up. We can provision a locked sandbox in our hosted environment within 24 hours for Phase 1; it will mirror the production runtime but with capped throughput and no persistent storage. For the Phase 1 smoke we propose the following acceptance criteria (I put the same list in evaluation_plan_v2.pdf):

- Ingest: 50k synthetic rows processed with end-to-end latency < 150ms p50 and < 600ms p95.
- Accuracy: matching baseline intent/slot extraction >= 92% on the sample prompts provided.
- Stability: no service-level errors > 1% over the 3-day run.

Operational notes: we will run a KV cache warm-up pass before the smoke to avoid cold-start artifacts; log bundles will be shared via our secure Drive link. If Phase 1 passes, we will hand over a VPC-template and runbooks for Phase 2 onboarding.

Attachments: evaluation_plan_v2.pdf (detailed runbook, metrics capture), I'll also upload the initial log parser to the shared Drive.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin | Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Megan Torres <megan@borealis.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-24T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Close timeline failure-mode analysis and contingency actions

Megan — thanks for the phased approach suggestion, that works from a customer-success perspective and prevents a hard slip. Two commercial asks to keep in mind if we are formally re-baselining:

1) Commitment to exec alignment: if Borealis accepts Phase 1 and the PO is cut for Phase 1, we request an internal executive confirmation (email ok) committing to move to Phase 2 within 30 days of SOC2 delivery. That protects our sandbox scheduling.
2) If the close extends beyond 2028-07-05 for reasons outside Redwood's control (procurement/SOC2 delays), we will need a short-term billing accommodation (one-time credit or reduced trial overage). Not a blocker for us, but I want to surface it now so finance can provision an exception if required.

Action items I will own: produce a two-column MAP delta that lists new dates, owners, and acceptance criteria (will attach in the shared Drive by EOD). Markus — please confirm whether Redwood will host Phase 1 sandbox and accept the proposed acceptance criteria from Marcus.

—Laura
Laura Bennett | Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Megan Torres <megan@borealis.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-27T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Close timeline failure-mode analysis and contingency actions — escalation and owners

All — summary and escalation note for our execs (copying the updated risk log attached):

Decision: Redwood will provision the Phase 1 hosted sandbox (no customer PII) and run the 3-day smoke on 2028-06-29 to preserve runway. Marcus will lead the run (owner). Laura will circulate the MAP delta by EOD and Priyom will update our internal schedule and capacity allocation.

Risks & owners (logged in redwood-risk-log-20280621.csv):
- Procurement hold (external): Owner: Megan/Adam — risk of PO delay -> impact: slip to 2028-07-20+
- SOC2 artifact delivery (external): Owner: Adam — impact: Phase 2 cannot proceed until artifacts received
- Full-data ingest time (internal + external): Owner: Marcus — mitigation: reduced-scope ingest + throughput probe

Escalation ask: if Borealis cannot provide a conditional PO for Phase 1 by EOD 2028-06-28, I will escalate to our VP of Sales and request a brief executive procurement exception call with Borealis leadership to preserve the mutual close date.

Next steps:
- Marcus: sandbox ready 2028-06-28 18:00 PDT, run 06-29 to 07-01.
- Laura: MAP delta doc uploaded to Drive and HubSpot record updated.
- Priyom: capacity hold placed for the sandbox and finance briefed on potential credit.

Thanks — I will open the executive thread only if we hit the PO deadline without commitment.

—Markus
Markus Klein | Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-risk-log-20280621.csv
